paragraphs: This combined occupation turns drawings and site dimensions into wall or ceiling substrates and finishes: installers measure, cut, and secure panels, tapers tape, mud, and sand joints, and ceiling installers build the grid and install panels.
Suitable for a first try: likes seeing progress directly through dimensions and hands-on results; able to repeatedly carry, lift, secure, tape, and sand.
Choose carefully: not suitable for people who ignore the risks of heights, dust, and carrying.

Low-risk verification: complete the fictional exercise on this page and only judge whether you are willing to verify, record, and escalate; do not perform working-at-height installation, power cutting, carrying, or dust sanding; real projects must be verified against drawings, codes, and site conditions.

This page is a bounded combination of two official exact O*NET occupations: 47-2081.00 drywall and ceiling tile installers measure, cut, and secure wallboard or ceiling panels; 47-2082.00 tapers seal panel joints, tape, apply joint compound, and sand or repair surfaces.
Real inputs include construction drawings and room dimensions, studs and substrate, panels or ceiling tiles, openings and details, fasteners, joint materials, and site safety conditions.
Installers lay out and measure, cut and carry, and secure panels; ceiling workers arrange the suspension grid; tapers tape, apply joint compound in layers, sand, and repair.

Key judgments include panel layout and cutouts, joint locations, surface flatness, material waste, and stopping to coordinate when dampness, structural, mechanical and electrical, or fire protection detail conflicts are found.

The BLS OOH explicitly lists tape measures, straightedges, utility knives, and power saws, and notes that mechanical lifting equipment, ladders or scaffolding, trowels, and mechanical taping and finishing tools may be used; O*NET tasks support operations such as sanding. Specific equipment selection and safe use must be verified against the project, and software recruitment skills are not treated as evidence of physical tools.
Collaborators include the site supervisor, carpenters and light-gauge steel stud workers, electricians, plumbers, insulation and fire protection trades, painters, and quality inspectors.

Dimensions, fastening/panel joints, and surface and defect treatment are verified against the applicable design and system; these are not uniform acceptance parameters for this page. Mainland China ceiling GB50210-2018 chapter 7 verifies the design, materials/quality, concealed acceptance, and construction records; concealed items before panel closing include hangers/studs and internal piping and equipment. Reverse bracing is provided when the hanger length is >1500mm, and a steel transfer layer is provided for upper grids/steel roof frames or hangers >2500mm, all of which must be verified against the actual design and cannot be merged into the same threshold. GB55032-2022 has been in force since 2023-03-01 and is fully mandatory, and the new code prevails in case of conflict; the mandatory clauses listed in GB50210 such as 7.1.12 have been repealed, which is not the repeal of the whole standard. Design changes are issued as documents by the design unit and approved as required, and are not a drawing change made by the project manager alone.

Drywall and ceiling tile installer (47-2081): measures, cuts, and secures drywall or ceiling material, with installation precision and substrate quality as the delivery focus.
Taper (47-2082): handles joints, tape, and finishes to prepare for later surface completion; it is a different exact code from 47-2081.
Ceiling installation: although it can fall within the 47-2081 scope, the material system, suspension layout, and working-at-height context are more prominent.
Carpenters: cover broader wood structure, formwork, and component construction, with overlapping tools but different materials, drawing reading, and scope of responsibility.

Construction and maintenance painters: prepare and coat building surfaces, and the deliverable is a protective or decorative coating; they take over a completed substrate and do not have panel securing or joint leveling as their core.
Floor layers (47-2042): measure, cut, and lay resilient or decorative floor covering materials, and the material direction and substrate judgment differ from wall/ceiling panel installation.
